brief: Scotiabank's week-ahead previews five threads. US payrolls: August's 162k gain reflected a seasonal-adjustment jump (would have been 15k under last year's factor) plus one-off drivers (40k weather effect, 35k government hiring, 62k leisure/hospitality) that left the rest of the labor market at ~25k; the author forecasts September payrolls +75k, unemployment steady at 4.1%, with downside risk, though the FOMC has deemed the labor market fine and is focused on inflation instead. Canada: Q2 GDP grew 3.3% q/q SAAR, hours-worked strength points to a further ~2% q/q Q3 pace; with inflation at or above the BoC's 2% midpoint and the output gap closing within 1-2 quarters, Scotiabank argues the BoC is already behind and should hike toward the upper end of its 2¼%-3¼% neutral range, making October 28 a live meeting. The RBA is expected to hike to 4.6% Tuesday on above-target inflation; BanRep is expected to hold at 12% but a hawkish minority could force a surprise hike. US PCE, Eurozone CPI and Tokyo CPI feed the Fed's, ECB's and BoJ's next moves respectively.
